mechanism_narrative: Sustained contraction in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last two weeks reflects a broad withdrawal from commuting and public-space activity that removes incidental footfall from retail corridors, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -24.3 to -35.7 between t-2w and t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES fell from -24.1 to -40.6 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is greater than or equal to the last 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both declined over the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES greater than 5 points crosses a compliance threshold that makes stay-at-home directives salient, causing households to cut non-essential retail trips and lowering RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 7.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Following a week when WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points, RETAIL_REC is higher the next week than the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT is deeply negative and RESIDENTIAL is simultaneously at or above baseline, the interaction indicates voluntary avoidance of public spaces rather than workplace mandates alone; this avoidance suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -30 and RESIDENTIAL above 0.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.7 and RESIDENTIAL at 1.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks with TRANSIT below -30 and RESIDENTIAL above 0.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a spring seasonal reopening regime, a shallower PARKS decline signals increased outdoor activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -25.7 at t-1w to -21.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS is above -22, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in GROCERY_PHARM from -14.4 to -22.1 indicates reduced essential errands and household withdrawal from routine shopping, which precedes a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 7.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the week following a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM decline of more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC reaching -40.0, its most negative value in the four-week window, crosses a policy pain threshold that triggers relaxed restrictions or renewed retail adaptation, producing a higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC at or below -38 for one week
failure_condition: After RETAIL_REC is at or below -38, its next 14-day mean is not higher than its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM indicate broad withdrawal from public and routine spaces; their interaction amplifies the retail contraction and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: When both TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM are below their t-2w values, RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is not lower than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL above baseline while WORKPLACES is severely negative indicates stabilized remote-work routines; as households adapt, local errands and neighborhood retail recover, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: In weeks with RESIDENTIAL above 1.0 and WORKPLACES below -35, RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is not higher than its last 28-day mean.
